correctness.rationale: For a Q=q² by L=q(q+1) point-line incidence matrix B, BB^T=qI+11^T; the adjacency A has five eigenspaces with eigenvalues ±sqrt(q(q+1)), ±sqrt(q),0. The source explicitly constructs orthogonal projectors, and sink-restricted principal 2x2 Grams give nonprincipal rank 2 for all sink pairs at q>=3 except point-point zero mode absent; two line zero-mode Gram has rank 1 for parallel lines and rank 2 for intersecting lines. Positivity follows from determinants (q-1)²/q², (q²-q-1)/q², (q-2)/q etc.; all are strictly positive where needed. The bright complement is invariant and loss-free, while any nondecaying bright eigenvector contradicts being simultaneously annihilated at both sinks; finite-dimensional decay proves capture is the bright projector diagonal independent of sink rates. Incident point-line substitutions in inverse Gram matrices yield site laws and trace D=7. Independently built GF(3) and GF(5) prime affine-plane incidence, diagonalized full A, and compared all 210 + 1485 sink pairs and mixed incident histograms; all matched. Numerical tests do not prove non-Desarguesian cases; universal incidence identities do. No claims for Laplacian, finite-time, noisy or additional-sink dynamics.
